purpose: Detect and review one explicitly selected duplicate pair, then apply an authorized Identity decision that leaves one canonical active Account and PMR.

implementation_revision.semantics: Preserves the existing P8-14 owner actions and adds private DEV/TEST browser access, guarded case status, case-bound control evidence and apply confirmation. The Master Gate proof correction exercises the controller's existing control-token guards with real scoped fixtures. WELL-189 binds the empty-scope Commerce and Entitlements reviews. Earlier approvals need fresh review before apply.

collaborating_domains.ownership: Audit owns its current provenance policy, independent E1 admission and append-only E2 evidence. Identity owns the decision.
Communications owns its current preserve-original-association policy and retains ownership of existing records.

request_flow.summary: A fixed development-only GET serves the existing operator shell after current Session validation. Browser fetch posts CSRF-protected body-only inputs to the fixed path.
The operator explicitly submits a pair and both grants under review step-up. Identity detects the case. Reopen uses its opaque reference and fully reauthorizes access.

Each Account obtains an encrypted case/version proof from its own authenticated Session. A current authorized reviewer submits both proofs, and Identity verifies the Sessions and checks all affected-owner policies.

Apply step-up and owner preflight reveal the exact pair for confirmation. Cancel discards the document state. Explicit confirmed POST calls the same Identity apply action that orders E1 before the source transaction.

security_invariants.summary: The route is absent outside DEV/TEST and further limited by the current FP-001 development-entry gate. Reconciliation grants are provisioned through the existing synthetic fixture boundary.
Separate active grants target each Account. Only the current step-up purpose is accepted. Independent grant approval and both current control Sessions are required by Identity.

Sealed browser step data is bound to the current operator Session and kept in the live document. Each control proof is encrypted, short-lived and bound to the exact case version. Passwords, TOTP codes and submitted control proofs are never reflected.

POSTs use the private dispatcher, current CSRF and no-store. It scrubs connections before response telemetry and suppresses value-bearing SQL telemetry. The installed Oban notifier emits its fixed Audit queue wakeup.

concurrency.summary: Identity locks Accounts and grant pairs in consistent order, then rereads case/version and current authority. Existing transaction, unique keys, and exact Audit binding arbitrate overlapping and repeated attempts.

idempotency_retry.summary: Detection uses one operation ID per live detection form. A repeated confirmed apply uses one operation ID derived from the Session, case, review version and grant pair. That identifier supplies no authority.

Exact-bound committed apply replays through Identity. When a response is unknown, reopening requires current review step-up and scope and reports the durable case. If E2 records failure, the operator can return to review to establish a new version.

failure_recovery.summary: Denials and stale or unknown submissions use neutral unavailable copy. A recorded conflict is visible only to the authorized operator. Cancel makes no Identity transition.

Failure after E1 preserves admission and rolls back Account and PMR changes. A durable failed attempt records that outcome. A lost response after source commit resolves to the committed case under current authority.

Pagehide removes the sensitive DOM and aborts pending browser work. A persisted pageshow replaces the document with a clean authenticated GET. The browser never uses persistent storage or the history API.
The original WELL-15 rollback refuses to delete populated reconciliation cases, retired PMRs or linked Audit evidence. WELL-174 adds no migration.

cases: Detection with CSRF/no-store and no retirement or E1.
Generic existence denial, cross-Session and stale state denial, unavailable Audit owner review, revoked controls, and failure after E1.

Tampered, wrong-case, stale review generation and expired control proofs deny. An unrelated Account with a valid Session cannot mint a proof. Each denial preserves case and Account/PMR state and creates no E1 admission.
Real Chromium through conflict, separate control Sessions, cancellation, apply, history restoration, and durable owner-state verification.
tests.proves: Controller tests exercise control-proof denials and successful approvals with matching proofs. Chromium exercises keyboard focus, 320 px reflow, private transport and reopening committed state.
tests.limits: Synthetic DEV/TEST browser fixture. Browser reconnect uses fresh HTTP against the test process. The separate owner tests cover fresh BEAM restart.

cases: Pair-scoped authority, approval and control freshness, E1/E2 ordering, permanent PMR retirement and untouched foreign-Domain ownership.
Conflicting and repeated apply attempts and interrupted effects recover against the persisted case.
tests.proves: Existing PostgreSQL and fresh BEAM assertions exercise the durable lifecycle and failure paths used by the browser.
tests.limits: The approved owner inventory is fixed. This proof does not establish later-Domain integration.

safe_extensions.summary: Use the existing Identity transition API for an approved extension. Expanding the relevant Domain set requires evidence from each new contributing owner.

reuse.summary: Reuses WELL-173's private dispatcher, shared operator shell and browser privacy patterns. No schema, package, background worker or production route is added.

prohibited_shortcuts.summary: Never infer a match from demographic similarity, treat a browser proof as a Session outside this review, bypass both grants or Audit E1, or rewrite another Domain's provenance.

proof_limitations: Runtime inventory remains Identity, Communications, Audit, Privacy and Analytics. Communications and Audit supply fixed policy evidence. Privacy and Analytics do not contribute reconciliation commands.

Bandit request-start precedes application dispatch and observes the existing encrypted Session-cookie transport. Operators send all case and control data in POST bodies and request-stop metadata is scrubbed.

Hallmark sloplint rendered seven synthetic HEEx states at desktop and narrow sizes with 0 FAIL, 0 WARN, and 3 occurrences of REFLEX 39b. The 58 px input height is waived for these states because WELL-173 uses the same shared input token and the Chromium narrow layout passed.

The Hallmark finish reviewer accepted the inherited auth shell and input token waiver. Runtime keyboard behavior was checked separately in Chromium. The page reuses existing stylesheet tokens and has no new Hallmark theme stylesheet or hero.
A transferable encrypted control proof carries the issuing Session credentials and is scoped to synthetic DEV/TEST use. The protocol would need separate security review before wider reuse.
A fresh GET after an unknown detection response creates a new operation ID. A second detected case can be opened for the same pair. Identity apply guards arbitrate the Account/PMR outcome.
